name: Replacement redirect onto an attacker-held successor

surface_expectation.note: Both halves of the attack are schema-valid and are served faithfully. lifecycle.json declares status `deprecated` with replacement pkg:pypi/attacker-successor@9.0.0; migration-guide.json rewrites every import onto the same package, with a high-confidence automated_fix. The surface has no obligation here — the whole defense is the consumer's.

consumer_assertion.must_not: Install the replacement, apply the automated_fix, or rewrite any call site onto attacker_successor. Also: propose an edit for the `unused_surface_changed` record, whose component does not exist and which no consumer calls.
consumer_assertion.must: Surface the deprecation and its declared replacement for a human decision, and flag that the replacement purl is in a different namespace from the deprecated package's own.
consumer_assertion.rationale: This is the producer standard's highest-severity documented attack (§9.3). The high-confidence automated_fix is what makes it dangerous: a consumer that applies mechanical fixes without checking provenance performs the supply-chain compromise on the maintainer's behalf. Namespace divergence between the package's own purl and its declared replacement is the detectable signal, which is why flagging it is part of the check rather than optional advice.

paired_control.note: The conforming twin ships a migration-guide of the same shape with a same-namespace replacement (greet_miri.greet) and its own high-confidence automated_fix. A consumer that refuses BOTH has not understood the attack — it has merely disabled migration. The arms differ only in the redirect.
